references.id: UK Treaty Series 29 (1926), Cmd. 2777
references.operator: United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office treaty archive
references.document_date: Signed at Cape Town 1926-06-22; presented as Treaty Series No. 29 (1926)
references.relevant_content: Articles 1-3 resolve the Ruacana/Rua Cana waterfall identification and describe the Angola–South-West Africa line from the falls along the latitude parallel to the middle of the Okavango/Cubango, then by reference to the 1886 Lisbon treaty. Article 4 requires joint demarcation and specified beaconing/astronomical observation. Article 6 says the river middle line applies where the line follows a river and cuts an island.
references.scope_limit: Primary treaty text supports the described boundary framework. It does not itself provide a modern georeferenced coordinate polyline or the underlying completed demarcation record for these candidate polygons. The source line at issue is inland; the later 2002 maritime treaty is irrelevant.

references.id: JRC Global Surface Water v1.5 Occurrence 1984-2024
references.operator: European Commission Joint Research Centre / Google

references.relevant_content: The official guide defines occurrence as month-normalized frequency of surface-water detections from March 1984 through December 2024; values 1–100 represent percentage and 0 means not water. references.use_limit: Occurrence is a long-term summary and does not date detections. The dataset describes a spatially variable residual co-registration offset at the 2022 Landsat Collection 2 transition, generally sub-pixel but at or above one 30 m pixel in some path/rows. It does not establish a specific bank, waterbody type, legal boundary, processing cause, or territorial assignment. Attribution: Source: EC JRC/Google.

references.id: UK Treaty Series No. 28 (1931), Cmd. 3896; enclosed 1928 Final Act and Beacon schedule
references.operator: United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office treaty archive
references.document_date: Exchange of Notes Lisbon 1931-04-29; enclosed South-West Africa–Angola Boundary Demarcation Commission Final Act signed at Kakeri 1928-09-23.
references.relevant_content: The 1928 Final Act states the line was defined by chords joining 47 main beacons, starting on the left bank of the Kunene at Oruahakana/Ruacana Falls and ending at Beacon 47 at Kakeri on the Okavango. The schedule gives Beacon 47 at 17°23′23.7″ S, 18°25′06.2″ E and describes it on a limestone ridge 240 m west of the river bank. It reports astronomical observations at intervals no greater than 50 km and beacons no greater than 10 km apart. The 1931 exchange records the Union Government’s acceptance of the demarcation/description, and the Portuguese reply states that the exchange of notes shall be considered the instruments of ratification of the 1928 Kakeri Agreement and its annexes.
references.use_limit: This is primary evidence of the historical demarcation and its scheduled endpoint. It does not provide georeferenced 1928 river midstream geometry east of Beacon 47, establish current beacon condition, or decide present legal effect. All 21 candidate geometry bounds lie east and south of Beacon 47; their relation to the treaty’s river-midstream line remains unresolved.

references.id: GLAD Global Surface Water Dynamics, tiles 10S_010E and 10S_020E, 1999–2023 objects
references.operator: Global Land Analysis and Discovery / University of Maryland; Google Cloud Storage public objects
references.retrieval_status: All 74 generation-pinned COGs (25 annual percent layers and 12 monthly climatologies for each of two tiles) downloaded, checked against GCS size and MD5 and SHA-256 hashed; 2,383,301,892 bytes total. Original raster bytes are in the local review cache rather than Git; the packet records object generations and hashes and includes a re-download/verification script. The actual object inventory ends at 2023 even though the product page currently advertises through 2025.
references.relevant_content: The 30 m, EPSG:4326 pixel-center analysis finds at least one >=50% water-classified center in each of the 21 candidates in every annual layer 1999–2023, and in 39 of 49 positive-area candidate/contact intersections in at least one year. The analysis JSON was reproduced byte-identically twice.
references.use_limit: A distinct classification product using Landsat 5/7/8/9, not an independent sensor family from other Landsat-derived water products. No per-pixel observation counts are supplied. Annual percentages and month-of-year climatologies cannot date individual detections or establish a 1928 watercourse/bank. Mixed pixels, seasonal vegetation, observability, registration and the 30 m grid limit interpretation.

references.id: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 10 m annual land-cover classification
references.operator: ESA WorldCover consortium
references.retrieval_status: Two source COGs covering all 21 candidates and the 49 positive-area candidate/contact intersections were retained from the official 2021 v200 dataset path. Full source-file SHA-256 hashes and dimensions are included in worldcover-2021-analysis.json. Output was reproduced twice byte-identically using source pixel centers from the original EPSG:4326 affine grid.
references.use_limit: Annual 2021 land-cover labels, not dated water observations or shoreline/bank vectors. Product classification is partly based on Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2; validation estimates are global and not candidate-specific. Per-geometry center counts are not deduplicated areas. A direct global-center mask is retained; comparison with Rasterio local window masks produced 61 differing center decisions across all 70 analyzed masks, so boundary/mask sensitivity is disclosed.

references.id: AWS Sentinel-1 GRD COG archive / 2020 seasonal backscatter screen
references.operator: AWS Open Data Registry (public Sentinel-1 L1 GRD COG collection); Earth Search STAC catalog operated by Element 84
references.document_date: Scene acquisitions screened: 2015-09, 2018-08, 2020-03, 2020-08, 2025-03, 2025-08. STAC catalog records specify Sentinel-1 platform, acquisition datetime, orbit, polarization, scene footprint and asset metadata.
references.retrieval_status: In addition to six saved STAC coverage searches, six 2020 scene products from March 19/24 and August 10/15 were sampled in wet-season and dry-season windows, matched by relative orbit for each candidate. The 21 original candidates have sampled VV/VH backscatter in both windows. Of 49 positive-area candidate/contact intersections, 48 have at least one selected pixel center in both windows; the remaining positive-area intersection is too small to contain a pixel center. Nineteen candidate polygons are fully covered by their SAFE tiepoint-footprint unions; two have 99.7% and 99.9% planar coverage. The analysis is a signal-distribution screen, not a water classification.
references.use_limit: COG pixels are uint16 raw measurements; sigma0 distributions were calculated using ESA sigmaNought and noiseRangeLut annotations. However, every inspected COG TIFF ImageDescription says Sentinel-1A while the STAC item and SAFE missionId say Sentinel-1B; the COGs also carry no embedded CRS/geotransform. Geographic placement uses the SAFE tiepoint lattice, but the spacecraft-tag conflict and absolute registration remain unresolved. No DEM terrain correction, radiometric terrain normalization, speckle filtering, ground-truth validation, water mask, bank line, or historic channel inference was produced. Threshold fractions are sensitivity measures only.
references.scope: STAC search footprint intersection and coverage against all 21 immutable candidate polygons; no production geometry change and no administrative assignment.
references.calibration_reference: ESA Sentinel-1 Product Specification, issue 3/9, 2021-05-07, Sections 6.3.2–6.3.3; see separate reference record.

spatial_screen.method: Compare candidate latitude bounds with the approximate latitude stated for the 1926 Ruacana/Rua Cana Falls point; use only as a locator screen, not as a legal boundary test.
spatial_screen.interpretation: The candidate family lies close to and south of the approximate latitude associated with the treaty's Ruacana point, and extends east toward the Okavango/Cubango. This makes the 1926 line, the 1886 river sequence, the river's historical course, and demarcation records material. The approximate waterfall latitude and bbox are not enough to assign territory or answer authority.

separate_classifications.consumed_source_geometry: Source products overlap candidate footprints by positive area; see source-geometry-comparison.json.
separate_classifications.current_physical_water_or_historic_cours: JRC GSW v1.5 provides separate 1984–2024 occurrence and 2024 seasonality observations at approximately 30 m; positive water-classified pixels occur within all 21 candidates. This supports water occurrence within the candidate footprints, not exact shoreline/current course or historical channel location. Waterbody type, floods/wetlands, collection-transition geolocation shift, and suitability for any legal line remain limits. ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 independently adds 10 m Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 annual land-cover classes: class 80 occurs in all 21 candidate masks and 38/49 positive-area overlaps; class 90 occurs in all 21 and 44/49 overlaps. Class 80/90 occurs in 46/49 overlaps. This supports class presence in 2021 labels only; it is not exact bank or historic-course evidence.
separate_classifications.processing_cause: Unresolved; no exact processing defect has been reproduced.
separate_classifications.international_boundary_authority: The 1926 agreement gives a treaty framework and requires joint demarcation, with archival catalogue leads for 1927–28 survey/commission records. Those underlying survey and beacon records are not inspected. Exact demarcated/current alignment across the candidate coordinates remains unresolved.
